entries.title: Exodus 25:1
segments:
We come not to the tabernacle and its furniture.  To guard against any intermixture of heathenish usages, as well as to impress upon the minds of the Israelites the truth that all acceptable worship of God must be in accordance with the rules of his appointment, Jehovah gave to Moses in the mount specific directions for the structure of the tabernacle and every thing pertaining to its service.  He showed him, moreover, a pattern, by which he was enabled at once to apprehend the meaning of all the directions he received, and to write them out in full, as is done in this and the six following chapters. 
 
The tabernacle was God's visible dwelling place.  As such it represented to the Israelites the great truth that Jehovah dwells spiritually with his people as their king and protector.  Thus the tabernacle, with all the services belonging to it, was "a shadow of good things to come."  It typified the higher blessings of the Christian dispensation, as is fully shown in the epistle to the Hebrews.

entries.title: Exodus 25:2
segments:
That giveth it willingly; thus God taught the people that he will have willing worshippers. 
 
God most justly requires of men that, whatever they do, they should seek to honor him and benefit their fellow-men.

entries.title: Exodus 25:4
segments: Blue, and purple, and scarlet; these colors were employed as being the most excellent.

entries.title: Exodus 25:5
segments:
Badgers' skins; according to some, the original word means the skin of a species of seal. 
 
  Shittim-wood; a species of acacia, an exceedingly fine and durable wood.  Gum arabic is obtained from the living tree.

entries.title: Exodus 25:7
segments: The ephod--breastplate; see the description of these,

entries.title: Exodus 25:8
segments: Though God is in all places, yet he dwells especially in those which, according to his will, are consecrated to his worship; and from them he bestows peculiar blessings on his people.

entries.title: Exodus 25:10
segments: An ark; this is a different word in the Hebrew from that rendered ark in

, and means a chest. 
 
  A cubit; about eighteen inches.

entries.title: Exodus 25:11
segments: A crown; a cornice or border around the lid of the ark.

entries.title: Exodus 25:13
segments: Staves; poles or rods to go through the rings of the ark, by which to carry it.

entries.title: Exodus 25:16
segments:
The testimony; the tables of stone, on which were written the ten commandments, God's testimony as to the duty of men. 
 
What relates to the worship and glory of God, and to the redemption of men by Jesus Christ, is described in the Bible with greater minuteness, and treated as of greater importance, than the temporal interests of kingdoms, or all the mere worldly concerns of men.

entries.title: Exodus 25:17
segments: A mercy-seat; this was the golden covering or lid, the upper side of the sacred chest or ark, called the mercy-seat because on it was sprinkled the blood of atonement, and above it dwelt Jehovah in his visible glory, dispensing mercy to men.

entries.title: Exodus 25:18
segments: Cherubim; representations of creatures intensely studying, for the purpose of doing the will of God.  Some have supposed them to resemble the living creatures described

entries.title: Exodus 25:20
segments: One to another; the cherub on one end looking towards the cherub on the other end of the mercy-seat, both looking towards the mercy-seat, and their wings stretched over it.
.  Between them, on the mercy-seat, was the shekinah, or the visible glory of Jehovah.  Hence, he is said to dwell between the cherubim.

entries.title: Exodus 25:22
segments: All things which, by divine appointment, are connected with the sanctuary, were designed by god to impress upon the worshippers a conviction of his presence, and communicate something of those truths which relate to the bestowment of mercy and the gift of salvation through Christ.

entries.title: Exodus 25:24
segments: A crown; cornice or rim.

entries.title: Exodus 25:25
segments:
Border; this was to be below the leaf, around the frame of the table. 
 
  Handbreadth; the width of the four fingers; about three or four inches. 
 
  A golden crown; a rim of gold around the border, like that around the leaf of the table.

entries.title: Exodus 25:29
segments:
Spoons; or bowls. 
 
  Covers; or cans. 
 
  To cover withal; better, to pour out withal.

entries.title: Exodus 25:30
segments: Show-bread; twelve loaves of bread, equal to the number of the tribes.  It was placed on the table, and called show-bread, or bread of the presence, because it always stood in the presence of the Lord.  It was sprinkled with frankincense.  On the Sabbath the bread was taken away, and new bread put in its place.  The frankincense that was on it was burnt as an oblation to God, and the bread was eaten by the priests.
.  On one emergency mentioned in Scripture it was given to others.

.  This show-bread, and all the articles and worship in the tabernacle, and afterwards in the temple, pointed forward to the Bread of God, which was to come down from heaven, and give life unto the world.

. 
 
It is not enough, in order to salvation, that Christ tasted death for every man, and was made a propitiation for the sins of the world; but in order to be saved, men must receive from him spiritual life, be united to him, and receive from him permanently spiritual nourishment and support.

entries.title: Exodus 25:31
segments:
A candlestick; it consisted of an upright shaft, with six branches coming out in pairs, three on each side, making a line of seven lamps. 
 
  Knops; knobs or embossed work.  These and the bowls and flowers were ornamental figures on the shaft and branches.

entries.title: Exodus 25:33
segments:
Like unto almonds; in the form of an almond. 
 
  In the six branches; three bowls, knobs, and flowers on each branch, and four on the shaft of the candlestick, making twenty-two in all.

entries.title: Exodus 25:35
segments: Of the same; the same material, pure gold.

entries.title: Exodus 25:37
segments:
Seven lamps; one for the shaft, and one for each branch of the candlestick. 
 
Jesus Christ is the light of the world.  All men, and especially his ministers, are bound to follow him, that they may not walk in darkness, but have the light of life; and to let that light so shine in godly, beneficent conduct, that men shall be led to glorify their Father in heaven.

entries.title: Exodus 25:38
segments: The tongs; snuffers or scissors to trim the lamps.

entries.title: Exodus 25:39
segments: A talent of pure gold; estimated by some to be equal to about twenty, and by others, thirty thousand dollars.  The light of these lamps represented the spiritual light which God in Christ, by his word and Spirit, through the instrumentality of his people, especially his ministers, communicates to the world.
